key_insight: A polymorphic high-entropy oxide photocatalyst paired with microalgae as a sacrificial agent significantly boosts solar-driven CO2 conversion to CO and CH4 while adding a carbon-negative capture step.
engineering_relevance: This work suggests a practical route to improve photocatalytic CO2 utilization by co-designing catalyst chemistry, surface basicity, and a sustainable biomass-based feedstock.
method: Used Cs/Ba to enhance CO2 chemisorption and Bi to promote polarization/charge separation
Compared CO2 conversion under three conditions: HEO alone, with microplastics, and with microalgae
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 10× higher CO and 4× higher CH4 production with microalgae compared with the HEO-only system.
watch_item: The result is promising, but scalability and stability of microalgae-assisted photocatalysis under real outdoor operating conditions remain to be demonstrated.
paper_title: Sustainable photocatalytic CO2 conversion using microalgae as a carbon-negative scavenger
